sec3.successToast: Your request has been sent successfully!

asilbek.description: I got IELTS 9.0 three times in a row, and honestly, none of it happened by accident. Every session I run is built around one idea — impossible is a word people use before they've tried hard enough. I break down every skill into something manageable, track your weak points relentlessly, and push you past the plateau most students get stuck at. My students don't just pass the exam, they walk out speaking with real confidence. If you're ready to put in the work, I'll make sure the result follows.

ruxillo.description: Ruhillo started learning English on his own while still in school, and within just a few years became one of the most sought-after teachers in his city. He specializes in IELTS preparation and speaking practice, breaking down complex grammar topics into simple, easy-to-understand explanations. Over 4 years of teaching, he has prepared more than 200 students who scored IELTS 7 or higher, and he continues refining his own teaching methodology.

zarnigor.description: Zarnigor scored 8.5 on the international IELTS exam at just 17 years old, a remarkable achievement for her age. She holds a CELTA certificate and specializes in developing speaking skills and refining pronunciation. Zarnigor believes every student can reach a high result if the material is explained clearly and with patience, and that's exactly the approach she brings to every lesson.

gulasal.description: Gulasal holds the maximum IELTS score of 9.0 and a TESOL certificate, qualifying her to teach English at an international level. Over 5 years of practice, she has prepared more than 600 students, many of whom successfully entered universities abroad. Gulasal focuses on academic writing and confident spoken English, helping students not just pass the exam but truly master the language.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Check out the answers to the most common questions from our students.
faq.q1: How long do your courses last?
faq.a1: Depending on the direction, our courses last from 3 to 12 months. Classes are held 4 times a week by qualified teachers.
faq.q2: What is required to start classes?
faq.a2: To get started, you only need a laptop (computer), necessary books, internet, and a strong desire. Basic knowledge is taught from scratch.
faq.q3: What happens if I miss a class?
faq.a3: Active participation in every class is recommended. If you miss a class or struggle with a topic, our experienced assistant teachers will help you outside of class times, explaining the topics again and assisting with practical exercises.
faq.q4: Will I get a certificate after completing the course?
faq.a4: Yes, graduates who successfully complete the course will receive a special certificate, and the best students will receive practical help in finding a job.
faq.a5: Course prices vary depending on your level and whether you choose group or individual lessons. For precise information, please visit the pricing page or contact us.
faq.q6: What days are the classes held?
faq.a6: Classes are held 3 days a week with 1 additional day for the Speaking Club. You can choose a time that suits you best.
faq.q7: Is there a free trial lesson?
faq.a7: Yes, the first trial lesson is completely free for all new students at our center. This allows you to get acquainted with the learning process and the teacher.
faq.a8: Homework is strictly checked by teachers and their assistants before each lesson. Since not doing homework negatively affects the learning process, we take it very seriously.
faq.a9: Of course, we offer both traditional offline and online classes. Online classes are just as interactive and effective as offline ones.
faq.a10: If you do not understand the teaching style or wish to switch to another group, you can freely change your teacher or schedule by contacting our administration.

principles.p1_desc: Through our specially designed intensive programs, you will achieve noticeable results in language learning in a short time. Our methodology saves your time and ensures quality education.
principles.p1_f1_desc: With more weekly class hours and enriched learning materials, you will master the language quickly.
principles.p1_f2_desc: To save your time, we teach only the most relevant and necessary strategies that will appear on the exam.
principles.p1_f3_desc: Daily homework assignments and vocabulary memorization processes are strictly monitored by teachers.
principles.p1_extra_desc: Thanks to this fast methodology, our students usually reach their target IELTS 7.0+ or CEFR B2/C1 levels within 3-4 months. There is no magic – just hard work and proper guidance.
principles.p2_desc: The main part of our classes is focused on live communication and speaking skills, which helps you quickly overcome the language barrier and express your thoughts freely.
principles.p2_f1_desc: In classes, you don't just memorize rules, but learn how to apply them in practice. We unlock your speech through weekly speaking clubs.
principles.p2_f2_desc: Practice is not just about speaking, but also about taking tests. You will feel the atmosphere of a real exam during classes.
principles.p2_f3_desc: By listening to audios with various accents, you will be prepared not only for the exam but also for real-life communication.
principles.p2_extra_title: Practice is the Key to Success
principles.p2_extra_desc: Our center operates on the '20% Theory, 80% Practice' rule. You cannot get a high score just by knowing the rules; it is important to be able to apply them automatically.
principles.p3_desc: Individual work is carried out on the mistakes and shortcomings of each student. In addition, students regularly take mock tests, which constantly leads to high results.
principles.p3_f1_desc: Even if you study in a group, your personal mistakes will be deeply analyzed, and advice will be given on how to correct them.
principles.p3_f2_desc: Through standard Mock Tests conducted every month, you will track your level and growth dynamics.
principles.p3_f3_desc: We develop skills to overcome exam anxiety and allocate time properly, so that you are confident on the day of the exam.
principles.p3_extra_desc: There is no limit to perfection. Our goal is not just to help you pass the test, but to make English a part of your life.

ieltsWriting.p1Prompt: Some people think that mobile phones should be banned in schools, while others believe they are useful educational tools. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
ieltsWriting.p2Title: Task 1: Line Graph - Public Transport Passengers
ieltsWriting.p2Prompt: The line graph below shows the number of passengers using three types of public transport in a European city between 2000 and 2020. Summarize the main features and make comparisons.
ieltsWriting.p3Prompt: Online distance learning is replacing traditional classroom teaching in many universities. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?
ieltsWriting.p4Prompt: Some people believe that artificial intelligence will replace human workers in most industries, while others argue it will create new opportunities. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
ieltsWriting.p5Prompt: The bar chart compares the percentage of university graduates in six European countries who found employment within six months of graduation between 2010 and 2020. Summarize key trends.
ieltsWriting.p6Title: Task 2: Early Employment vs Higher Education
ieltsWriting.p6Prompt: Many young people prefer going directly into employment after high school rather than pursuing a university degree. Do the advantages of this trend outweigh the disadvantages?
ieltsWriting.p7Prompt: The diagram illustrates the process of purifying and recycling wastewater for domestic consumption. Describe the stages involved in this system.
ieltsWriting.p8Prompt: Should governments take sole responsibility for solving environmental issues, or should individuals change their lifestyle habits? Discuss both views and give your opinion.
ieltsWriting.p9Prompt: Providing a Universal Basic Income (UBI) to all citizens regardless of employment status is proposed as a solution to wealth inequality. Discuss the feasibility and potential consequences.
ieltsWriting.p10Title: Task 1: Pie Charts - Energy Generation 2005 vs 2035
ieltsWriting.p10Prompt: The pie charts show the proportions of energy generated from different sources in a developed nation in 2005 and projected figures for 2035. Summarize the main features and make comparisons.
ieltsWriting.p11Prompt: Due to globalization, many minority languages are dying out. Some argue that public money should be spent on preserving endangered languages, while others consider it a waste of resources. Discuss both views.
ieltsWriting.p12Prompt: The maps below show the town of Willington in 1995 and proposed redevelopment plans for 2025. Summarize the main features and make comparisons where relevant.
ieltsWriting.p13Prompt: The amount of money spent on space exploration is unjustifiable when there are so many problems on Earth. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
ieltsWriting.p14Prompt: The primary purpose of prisons should be to punish criminals rather than to rehabilitate them. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
ieltsWriting.p15Prompt: The diagram illustrates the stages of commercial coffee production, from harvesting beans to final packaging. Summarize the information by reporting the main features.

ieltsWriting.t1Instruction1: Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features.
ieltsWriting.t2Instruction1: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
